at a glance - the philippines improved its reading mathematics and science rankings in the programme for international student assessment - education officials emphasize the need to sustain this momentum and continue reforms manila philippines the philippines performance in the programme for international student assessment pisa improved in with the country climbing out of the bottom in the subjects covered the philippines ranked 72nd out of countries in reading 74th out of countries in mathematics and 77th out of countries in science according to the pisa results released on tuesday september the organisation for economic co-operation and development oecd which conducts the test found that filipino students had average scores of in science up by points from the previous pisa edition in mathematics up by points and in reading up by points the oecd described the philippines as the fastest improving country in terms of reading performance the department of education deped noted that this is the philippines strongest pisa performance to date since the country first joined the global assessment in and again in where it saw dismal results both times although an improvement it should be seen as a starting point and highlights the work that remains added the deped this is a significant achievement for our learners and for the entire philippine education system but more than the numbers we are seeing evidence that our learners are capable of making real and meaningful progress education secretary sonny angara said in a press release we should be proud of how far our learners and teachers have come but we should be even more determined about how much farther we can go in the philippines was ranked lowest in reading and second to the last in science and mathematics four years after that the philippines was still among the bottom the second congressional commission on education said the task now is to sustain the momentum stressing that education reforms require consistency of purpose continuity in implementation and the commitment of the entire country according to the oecd or around two in three filipino students were low performers in science mathematics and reading in in the edition the oecd also assessed students on computational problem solving or the ability of students to solve problems using modeling or programming tools and practices such as conducting experiments analyzing data and building and debugging computational artifacts the philippines scored below the oecd average of learning recovery in a press conference after the announcement angara attributed the improved pisa performance to deped reforms such as reducing the administrative work of teachers improving curricula and emphasizing remediation angara replaced vice president sara duterte as education secretary in he inherited sectoral issues such as poor performance of filipino students in global assessments low literacy rates and calls to either review or scrap the k to program pisa was conducted in the early stages of the academic recovery and accessible learning aral program the country s national learning recovery initiative but by the end of school year - or after the first full-year implementation of the aral program around half of filipino students were still not proficient in reading according to the deped s own literacy assessment angara said the first year of aral which focused on reading was very encouraging the deped is also preparing to roll out sessions for mathematics soon it s only the second year so let s iterate change the approach if we see things that need to be improved he said in a mix of english and filipino however under the current budget proposal the aral program may have zero funding in asked whether the pisa results could make lawmakers rethink the deped budget angara replied sana i hope so extra preparations after the poor performance in and the deped took extra measures to prepare for pisa read why philippines pisa preparation is flawed according to the deped around -year-old students from schools in the philippines took part in pisa through a computer-based assessment most of the participating schools were regular public schools but there were also public science-oriented schools and private schools angara said the deped made sure that public schools would have at least one computer so as education systems in all three subjects were estonia japan korea macau china chinese taipei and the united kingdom but while the philippines had encouraging results pisa recorded the lowest oecd-average performance observed so far in science reading and mathematics pisa shows that reversing declines in student performance is urgent the most successful education systems focus on fewer areas in greater depth invest in teachers engage parents and provide targeted support for the students and schools that need it the most oecd secretary-general mathias cormann said in a press release performance since joining the international test in angara said more than local government units lgus took part in preparations for pisa providing schools with resources and services intended to at a glance - the philippines showed significant improvement in the pisa results with increases in reading math and science scores attributed to intensive preparations by the department of education - despite these gains the country's scores remain low compared to oecd averages and a large percentage of students still fall below baseline proficiency levels highlighting ongoing educational challenges - the improvements were not evenly distributed with socioeconomically advantaged students seeing greater gains and concerns remain about the sustainability of these results and the overall learning crisis in the education system after a long wait on september we now have the results of the programme for international student assessment pisa which measures the skills of -year-old students there s good news all around philippine scores have improved in all three subjects tested our reading score rose from in to math from to and science from to all three increases were statistically significant meaning the analysis finds evidence of improvement beyond sampling and measurement uncertainty pisa noted that we were among eight participating education systems that exhibited significant gains in all three subjects great in addition the share of filipino students below baseline proficiency in science or pisa s minimum expected skill level also fell by a significant -percentage points between and all of this is welcome news and our teachers and students deserve recognition what accounts for the improvement on the one hand such a result should be hardly surprising given the intense preparations of the department of education deped president ferdinand marcos jr himself directed deped as early as to improve its pisa ranking in response deped formed a task force pisa whose job was to help teachers and especially students prepare for the computerized tests they provided computers to the hundreds of schools which would potentially be sampled at random by the pisa test administrators and took pains to allow students to practice on pisa-type reviewers so that they re less anxious to take the pisa test in case they are chosen to take it these were so-called familiarization sessions during test day itself deped also made sure to put in place a festive mood in the schools to make the exam less scary for students in deped also rolled out a special science program which involved teachers training their students in pisa-type questions this raised concerns that selected students were being trained for the sake of pisa a phenomenon called teaching to the test meanwhile within the deped hierarchy certain regional offices proferred incentives e g awarding of plaques in special events for pisa participating sdos and schools after the exam was administered the idea was to recognize the efforts and commitment of pisa-participating schools and prospectively incentivize continued improvement in learning outcomes to drive future enhancements in educational performance the singular focus of the public education system on pisa seems to have paid off the improvements are real but that s what you get from intense preparation as with any student determined to ace an exam preparation is key the philippines improvement is especially amazing given the broader trend in rich countries showing a significant deterioration especially in reading and math scores according to the official press release average reading scores fell by points across oecd countries between and equivalent to about one and a half years of learning mathematics scores fell by points equivalent to just over one year of learning among non-oecd pisa participants reading scores fell by points and mathematics scores by eight points over the same period whether this unsettling result is because of worsening digital distractions or greater use of ai we don t quite know yet at least for us we seem to be bucking this global trend for now beyond the headline gains of course there s much more to say about the philippines pisa results beyond the headline-grabbing gains first our reading score of is still quite low compared to the oecd average of in math the comparison is versus and in science versus our ranking in asean also still leaves much to be desired figure while we managed to overtake indonesia in reading and math the differences are not statistically significant cambodia managed to overtake us in science so that in the region we re now last in science vietnam which became an upper-middle income country this year like us is also way ahead of us in terms of math and science while the deped was gleeful to list the countries that now rank below us we cannot treat every country below us as a country we overtook some countries and economies below us in were absent in more troubling the vast majority of filipino students are still below the baseline proficiency level called level figure as much as are below-proficiency in reading in math and in science meanwhile of filipino students or nearly two in three were below baseline proficiency level in all three subjects simultaneously the gains were also unequal between and science scores rose by points among the most socioeconomically advantaged quarter of filipino students versus points among the most disadvantaged quarter the latter increase was not statistically significant while the gap widened by a significant points what worked what didn t naturally deped was in a self-congratulatory mood when the pisa results were announced but higher scores do not by themselves establish which specific deped program worked how much it contributed or which specific official deserves credit better instruction could have contributed alongside greater familiarity with the computer platform and question formats preparation can include actual teaching too which means learning and test preparation are not always separable the score increase alone cannot tell us how much came from each deped s preparation materials warrant scrutiny since we joined pisa resources already included computer-based familiarization and practice materials so these may have helped in the most recent round some people allege that deped handpicked good students and schools but pisa follows a prescribed sampling process and the oecd says philippine data met its quality standards the sample included students in schools nonetheless since deped knew weeks in advance which specific schools would participate it s worth asking did pisa-participating schools receive substantial extra support that comparable schools elsewhere did not till now we don t exactly know what happens after random selection and how much additional resources were poured to sampled schools maybe deped should publish the coverage timing and intensity of its preparations so that researchers can study their contribution establishing which measures helped would also inform whether they should reach more schools pisa s coverage has limits too the philippine sample represented about of the country s -year-old population leaving young people outside its coverage whose learning also deserves attention more research needs to be done a study published in the economics of education review studied vietnam s exceptional pisa performance despite being an emerging economy they found that vietnam s advantage persists even after adjustments for better-off students being overrepresented adolescents outside school being excluded and possible differences in test preparation and effort measured household and school characteristics explain only part of vietnam s exceptional performance and much remains unexplained for the philippines that study suggests that poverty alone need not determine educational outcomes researchers must find out how much of our learning gap persists after accounting for family circumstances and who gets tested and what could explain the remainder lingering learning crisis finally by no means do the new results tell us that we have eradicated our long-standing learning crisis apart from the learning poverty rate that previously shocked the country the second congressional commission on education edcom also reported that proficiency rates plummet from in grade abysmal as it already is to as low as by grade edcom s executive director karol mark yee also lamented recently on social media that the national government s budget documents for are replete with the phrase at least nearly proficient meaning that deped s performance indicators are considered met if students are at least nearly proficient not quite proficient karol argues that this is too low a bar and may serve to mask systemic underperformance on top of this education secretary sonny angara also divulged that for the budget proposed by the executive for the aral program amounted to zero aral involves remedial interventions for students lagging in reading as things stand there s also no budget yet to hire teachers next year worse the philippine center for investigative journalism pcij recently reported that politicians have made schools their milking cows as well they said data from the dpwh transparency portal reveals that contractors tied to the flood control scandal were the same ones awarded a large share of school infrastructure contracts moreover construction tycoons curlee and sarah discaya bagged some p13 billion worth of school building and facility contracts from to the largest haul among all contractors in sum let s celebrate the recent pisa gains but that should not lull us into thinking that the education crisis is now gone deped still needs to establish what caused the improvement and whether the measures behind it can help students across the country especially those who remain below baseline proficiency most importantly the deped must ensure that these gains are persistent and not just one-off rappler com jan carlo jc evaluate what is being read in mathematics the learner may solve more straightforward problems using fractions decimals percentages or measurement but may still struggle to apply these concepts
